lines.scene: INT. UPPER WEST SIDE APARTMENT - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You sure? We’re running a special on Vimtag Security Cameras. HD. You can access ‘em from your phone.

lines.scene: INT. UPPER WEST SIDE APARTMENT - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Course. And you got the Homelander watching over things. But, you know, the Homelander can’t be everywhere at once. Neither can the cops. HUGHIE (CONT'D) Or the nanny, for that matter. No, if we wanna keep an eye on our kids? That’s up to us. Even if we’re working long hours and late nights. Know what I mean?

lines.scene: INT. UPPER WEST SIDE APARTMENT - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Maybe you don’t need the cameras, but what about that one time you do? Is there such a thing as too safe?
Robin. That doesn’t mean what you think it means.

‘Laying pipe’ means sex. ‘Laying cable’ means you want me to come to your house and take a shit. ROBIN That’s disgusting. HUGHIE Hey, you said it. ROBIN You ready yet? Despite your best efforts, I’m still hungry.

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What can I say? I’m a good fucking salesman. Hey, I got you, didn’t I?

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Gary was totally supportive -- he just says things are slow. Next year, though, for sure.

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What do you want me to do? Go in there and kick his ass?

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: But you didn’t mean it. I see that look. C’mon, let’s hear it.

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Jesus. I didn’t realize you needed a sugar daddy.

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Wait. What’d you just say?

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hey. Don’t ever besmirch the Zeppelin poster.

lines.scene: EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
EXT. NEW YORK SIDE STREET - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: ROBIN! ROBIN!!

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - QUEENS - DAY
lines.dialogue: ...I’m not hungry. HUGHIE’S MOM Oh, honey. Look.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - QUEENS - DAY
lines.dialogue: Middle of the --? She was a half- step off the fucking curb.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - MINUTES LATER - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: But this -- is a confidentiality agreement.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - MINUTES LATER - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I sign this, I can’t talk about it? Have to pretend it didn’t happen? That I wasn’t holding Robin’s arms in my hands? DOUG FRIEDMAN I know you’re upset, but we’re just trying to help --

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - MINUTES LATER - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Then say you’re sorry --

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - MINUTES LATER - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You people say ‘condolences’ and ‘my regrets’ and ‘our sympathies,’ but no one can look me in the fucking eye and say “I’m sorry!” I’m not signing anything! Now get out!

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE’S FAMILY APARTMENT - MINUTES LATER - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I said GET THE HELL OUT! SMASH CUT TO: DOUG FRIEDMAN You okay? As I said, a boiler plate NDA, really pretty standard. HUGHIE I’ll think about it. DOUG FRIEDMAN Hughie -- HUGHIE Let me think about it. DOUG FRIEDMAN I get it. I’ll leave the document, gimme a ring if you have questions. You keep the pen, okay?
...so we can’t file criminal charges against A-Train. Heroes are like cops, they can’t be charged for collateral damage while in pursuit.
But -- but -- we can still file a civil suit. I found a lawyer -- he’ll work on percentage, won’t even charge us unless we win -- ROBIN’S DAD Hughie --
I just need you to jump in -- I’m not family, I can’t really sue by myself. But -- ROBIN’S DAD Hughie. Stop. We’re not suing anybody.
What? Why not? ROBIN’S DAD There’s no case. She was in the street. It’s the same as if she jay- walked and a bus hit her.
She was a half-step off the curb!

Wait, were they -- did you sign? You took their money? Gene? ROBIN’S DAD How long have I known you, Hughie? HUGHIE Since -- Robin and me were in high school. ROBIN’S DAD Prom night, actually. We met you, in that tux two sizes too big -- and there are some kids who just have that go-getter spark in their eye. You were not one of those kids. I’d say to her all the time, didn’t I? What’s Robin see in him? Got no drive, no fire, no fight. Boy doesn’t give a shit about anything. HUGHIE I cared about your daughter. I’m trying to fight now.
...no, you want the carbon cables. Cost more, but they conduct electricity way better --
You interested in a nanny cam? We’re running a special on Vimtag...
Sorry?
Uh, I -- I really don’t know.
Okay. Is there anything I can help you with?
I’m sorry, who are you?
I said who the hell are you? How do you know that?
You’re a Fed? You don’t sound like a Fed.
You don’t look like one, either.
Like a Columbine shooter.
Um. So what, exactly, can I do for you?
That can’t be true. That’s true?
C’mon. It’d be all over the news, people’d be screaming bloody murder.
Why?

lines.scene: INT. OLD MONEY BUILDING - PRIVATE CLUB - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hey, that’s Captain Fantastic. The ‘Capes for Christ’ guy. Holds those anti-gay rallies.

lines.scene: INT. OLD MONEY BUILDING - PRIVATE CLUB - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Okay. So this is more than I ever, ever wanted to see. I’m leaving now before one of them tries to have sex with me. Or kill me. Or both.

A-Train’s -- here? BUTCHER Was. This is from last night. BIG A-Train. Your girlfriend’s here. She’s pissed. BIG GAME She wants to know why you ran through her the other night. I mean, she just went to pieces. A-TRAIN Hey, I’m not the one that threw a Volvo at that carjacker, without realizing there was a fucking kid strapped inside. BIG GAME Screw you, man, that sucked. I had to go fucking cry on Diane Sawyer. A-TRAIN
...they’re laughing. Like she’s a joke. They’re fucking laughing.
They’re -- all like that? All of ‘em? Even the Homelander?
What are these?
Covering up -- what?
Or who was he running from? BUTCHER Yeah. True. Good point. Figure that out, we’ll have the fucker. Got a nose for this shit, and I’m tellin’ you, I can smell it. HUGHIE Okay. How can I help?
Wait, I don’t... why would I...?
So, sorry -- you want me to go into the Seven tower? By myself? And plant -- a bug? Like I’m fucking James Bond?
You gotta come with me.
What if something goes wrong?
Oh. Okay. Really comforting. And easy for you to say, as you sit out here on your “arse.” I mean, you’re FBI, if you’re fucking FBI, get a warrant, why do you need me --

Calm? You didn’t see A-Train, covered in Robin’s -- and I’m supposed to shake his hand and smile? These people kill fucking kids in fucking Volvos on, like, a random Tuesday, what do you think they’ll do to me if they catch me?
I said NO!
I just -- I can’t. I’m just gonna fuck it up. You won’t have your bug and I’ll be dead. I’m not like you.
I’m sorry, but... are you okay?
I know. Cloth handkerchief. I’m not really 90 years old, it’s just my Dad was in dry cleaning, he insists I carry -- never mind. Sorry to bother you.
That makes two of us. Work thing or life thing?
Life thing.
Mine’s not so hot...

Thing is, I -- I knew this girl. Who’d just -- charge headfirst into everything. Me, I backed away from everything, I was... I dunno... scared of falling or failing. But she’d say ‘just cause you fall on your ass, doesn’t mean you gotta stay there.’ So I guess I’d say the same to you. Pardon my french, but fuck those fuckers. Don’t give ‘em the satisfaction. You can still be a fighter -- just get up and fight.
I’m Hughie.
Hey. Hoping I’d find you here.
Okay. Let’s get A-Train.
I’ve got the -- I don’t know what ‘bottle’ means in that context, but I’m in, man, I wanna do this.
Yes.

lines.scene: INT. DIVE BAR - BY THE BATHROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: ...Mr. Friedman, got your message, and wow, 75k is -- life changing. I’ll sign whatever you want. I just -- I need one more thing. An apology from A-Train.

lines.scene: INT. DIVE BAR - BY THE BATHROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: No. He gave his regrets. And his sympathy. On TV. But I want him to look me in the eye and say he’s sorry.

lines.scene: INT. DIVE BAR - BY THE BATHROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Don’t think they’re going for it.
Hello? Yes, Mr. Friedman...?

lines.scene: INT. THE SEVEN TOWER - LOBBY - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hi -- are you Ashley? I’m Hughie Campbell...?

lines.scene: INT. THE SEVEN TOWER - LOBBY - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Uh -- sure.

lines.scene: INT. THE SEVEN TOWER - BOARDROOM - TWENTY MINUTES LATER
lines.dialogue: I need to -- go to the bathroom. Hello?

lines.scene: INT. THE SEVEN TOWER - BOARDROOM - TWENTY MINUTES LATER
lines.dialogue: Fine. I appreciate the apology. But accidents happen, right? And after all, you were saving the world.

lines.scene: INT. THE SEVEN TOWER - BOARDROOM - TWENTY MINUTES LATER
lines.dialogue: Where’s your bathroom?

lines.scene: EXT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL/INT. BUTCHER’S CAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: But you’re right -- fuck A-Train, fuck -- What’re we doing here?

lines.scene: EXT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL/INT. BUTCHER’S CAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I -- sorry?

lines.scene: EXT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL/INT. BUTCHER’S CAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What? But -- I don’t -- I mean, I can help you, let me help --

lines.scene: EXT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL/INT. BUTCHER’S CAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Um. Right. Okay.

lines.scene: EXT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL/INT. BUTCHER’S CAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Oh, hey, almost forgot -- ever see an asshole tear up 75k?

lines.scene: INT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL - NIGHT - LATER
lines.dialogue: Yeah, okay, thanks, Gary.

lines.scene: INT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL - NIGHT - LATER
lines.dialogue: Sorry. I’m closing up -- Hello?

lines.scene: INT. BRYMAN AUDIO VISUAL - NIGHT - LATER
lines.dialogue: The fuck? Where --

lines.scene: INT. BUTCHER’S CAR/EXT. BACK ALLEY - NIGHT - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Please! I don’t know what you’re talking about!
I don’t know! He was just a fucking Uber driver, okay?!
...please... please...
The TV!
Is he dead?
Shit. Shit. BUTCHER How’d you know electricity bollocksed the cunt? Took me forever to work that one out.
Skin’s carbon. Highly conductive. Saw it on ‘Ellen.’
Wait -- we what?
Me? You hit him! BUTCHER Semantics, my son, we’re both in a fucksight a’ trouble. HUGHIE No, he attacked us! And you’re -- you’re a federal officer! Call the fucking FBI!
I don’t know about this.
She hasn’t come after you yet.
What? I don’t -- I mean, of course I do, but not like, we’re just friends --
Oh my god. Oh my god.
You okay?
It’s got its charms. The rats are like Pokemon. With Hep-C.
It’s not so bad.
She saved you from the black site, remember Kimiko?
I know what you’re gonna say --
She has a lead on Stormfront.
What kinda breakthrough?

You -- want her to come? BUTCHER Naturally. Things go tits up, who do you think Vought’s after? Us or their billion dollar baby turned traitor who ripped out her own chip? Never go into shark infested waters without bringing chum. Cheers. NEWS With the House Judiciary Hearing into Vought just four days away, pro and anti Vought camps clashed in Manhattan this morning. Congresswoman Victoria Neuman said that Compound V must -- MAEVE (V.O.) This is who I am. Who are you? MAEVE (V.O.) Brave Maeve Pride Bars. Because you can’t be proud on an empty stomach.
Annie. If they recognize your face in there...
You see ‘em?
Guys, c’mon, not the time.
That’s enough --
Annie, stop!
You alright? Stormfront was there! MOTHER’S MILK That ain’t all who’s here.
Well, she just left. Get the hell out. MOTHER’S MILK On our way.
What the fuck?? BUTCHER Bloody hell, M.M., pick up!
Mom?
What... what happened?
Where’s Annie? STORMFRONT Hey -- you. Listen. I’m glad you’re here. I want to say how sorry I am. Just let me explain --
They’ve lost their minds.
You can’t just kill everyone.
You heard Mallory, she said if we can find another witness -- BUTCHER Right. I’ll bet they’ll be queuing up round the block after what happened to the last lot.
That won’t stop Vought. It won’t stop Compound V! You kill these Supes and Vought’ll just make a thousand more.
I’m 57 on the inside.
Just -- was the music in my house when I was a kid. I’d do somersaults to “You May Be Right” that were pretty thrilling to watch.
So it’s hopeless? Just kill ‘em all, let God sort ‘em out?
Then why are you even helping me?
They were gonna hurt you.
I just -- would never.
Hi. Hughie.
We’re all tired. They’re hurting people. Sooner or later, they’re gonna hurt someone you love.
New bling?
It’s fine.
My mom’s not dead.
She’s not dead. She left. When I was six.
It’s okay.

That’s... where the Billy Joel comes from. She and I would have these dance parties. She was fun. And she’d make awesome Seven costumes for Halloween. But then one day, she just left. Never called again. Not even a card. I heard she’s at an art colony in Minnesota?
Nope. It’s like a silent alarm went off and she was, like, fuck them, time to go.
What would you call it?
Guess that’s why I always just hang in there, no matter how bad it gets. Cause I don’t wanna be like her. Kinda clingy and pathetic, isn’t it?
What the FUCK?
I saved your life, asshole, and you’re coming after us?
Where’d you get it?
But -- why are you doing this?
I mean -- Becca! That’s incredible! We talked, she’s really great, she’s funny, you never told me how funny she was -- You’re really great.

No witness. But we definitely found fuck all, not sure I’m using that term properly. BUTCHER This’ll work just fine. So listen, you lot. Getting the kid back, it ain’t your fight, and I can’t ask you to come with -- MOTHER’S MILK Lick my big black balls. Sorry, Becca. We’ve spied and lied, done the nastiest shit for you. But this? The first good thing we’ve ever actually done? And you think we’re gonna take a pass? HUGHIE We’re in. FRENCHIE Of course we’re in.
Holy shit. It broke --
Wow. Catchy.
Look at you.
Congratulations on not being a fugitive.
Are you sure it’s safe for you to go back to the Tower?
Been thinking about that actually, the hanging in. And I think maybe I am too clingy.
Sticking with people just cause I’m terrified of losing ‘em? I can’t do it anymore. No, I gotta go off, stand on my own two feet for once.
Oh, God, no, I’m still clinging onto you! I’m not fucking crazy!
I can think of a way.
You can give me a job.

Don’t get me wrong, I still wanna fight Vought -- I just wanna do it the right way. Not covered in quite as many guts. Truth is, I never totally fit in with the guys. It’s time I stand on my own two feet.
I haven’t told them yet.
Holy shit. It broke --

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Fuck.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: No, I told you Vicky locked it all down, and please lower your voice.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: What the hell are you wearing?

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: I love it, it’s just, is now really the time? With the whole country barreling ahead to 1984?

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Okay...

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: I thought you weren’t ready. I mean, of course I want to marry you, but -- you kept saying it wasn’t the right time.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Stay right there, don’t move.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Annie January, I have loved you from the first time you kicked my ass with that triple strike in the eighth round.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - MAIN ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: You’re literally the nicest person in the city, all the other nice people should fuck off, and you’re right, I’m scared of what’s going to happen -- but I’m glad I get to face it with you.

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - BEDROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Wow. I, uh... that was surprising. Maybe next time, just the pinkie?

lines.scene: INT. HUGHIE AND ANNIE’S APARTMENT - BEDROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Where you going?

lines.scene: INT. HAZLET SAFE HOUSE - BUTCHER’S ROOM - INTERCUT
lines.dialogue: Where have you been? I’ve called you like fifteen times. I was worried, we thought you were...

lines.scene: INT. HAZLET SAFE HOUSE - BUTCHER’S ROOM - INTERCUT
lines.dialogue: Well, we’re kinda up against it. They’re a few hours from certifying the election, and then they’re coming for Singer -- we need your help tracking the Shifter, it’s all hands on deck.

lines.scene: INT. HAZLET SAFE HOUSE - BUTCHER’S ROOM - INTERCUT
lines.dialogue: Uh... huh.

lines.scene: INT. HAZLET SAFE HOUSE - BUTCHER’S ROOM - INTERCUT
lines.dialogue: Where are you? I’ll come to you --

lines.scene: INT. HAZLET SAFE HOUSE - BUTCHER’S ROOM - INTERCUT
lines.dialogue: Fine. I’ll... go to the topless steakhouse for you.

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: You seeing this? MOTHER’S MILK Get the dirt on Neuman ready in case we gotta go nuclear.

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: What about the virus?? MOTHER’S MILK There is no virus.

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: Shit! Y’know, she’ll kill us if we release this. MOTHER’S MILK If we had another fuckin’ choice, I’d take it.

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: What? No... no no no FUCK!!!!

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: Did Vicky send a virus? But how --

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: It’s all gone! Everything we had on Neuman: the murders, her links to Stan Edgar -- MOTHER’S MILK But you have backups -- another computer, the motherfucking Cloud!

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: You’re not hearing me, they’re gone. The originals, the backups, we’ve got nothing. MOTHER’S MILK Then there ain’t nothin’ stoppin’ her, only one thing left to do. You, stay here, work fucking faster. Kimiko, with me. Hughie -- I’m sending you coordinates. I need you and Annie there ASAP.

lines.scene: INT. THE TRUTHBOMB W/ FIRECRACKER SET - DAY
lines.dialogue: What’s the plan? MOTHER’S MILK We fucked our chance at offense. All we got now is defense.
You okay?
You should find some water.
Oh fuck.
Stay cool. It’s Annie. MOTHER’S MILK What’s Annie?
The Shifter, it’s Annie, she’s the Shifter! MOTHER’S MILK Are you sure? How do you know?

Trust me, I don’t know how or when they switched but that’s one hundred percent not Annie! MOTHER’S MILK Yo. The fate of the country literally depends on us keeping our shit tight right now, so chill. The fuck. Out.
Yep. Yes. We did that.

So true, the patriarchy needs to be pegged in all its holes... MOTHER’S MILK Congratulations! Getting hitched is the best decision I ever made. MOTHER’S MILK Anyway, I’m gonna hit the head, you guys hold down the fort --
SHIT!!!
How many fucking numbers are there??
You okay?
Thank God you showed up. How’d you find us, anyway?
She’s not -- wasn’t -- my fiancé.
I thought I was getting engaged to you! She looked just like you, down to that little freckle you have --
...I mean...
...had to be less than twenty.
She almost always initiated, and again -- cannot overstate this enough -- I thought it was you!

You know how I knew it wasn’t you? Cause she wore some designer dress, and you ditch your bra for sweats as soon as you’re home. She found your car keys on the first try and you have never found your keys in under fifteen minutes. But the final clue? She was sweating in the bunker and you have always been ninety percent Pashmina. I love that about you. All your weird fucked up-ness makes you, you. And you’re the one I want to spend the rest of my life with.
Vicky?
...is this a joke?
You’re only saying that because the assassination failed.
You’re like the asshole who cried wolf, I mean, the shit you’ve done --
Ah. So glad you two connected. Okay, the leg thing wasn’t me, but also, you didn’t leave us with a lot of choices --
I don’t know how to trust you.
Is she okay?
Maybe, but if we can flip Neuman to our side? As powerful as she is, with what she has on Vought? If there’s even a 5 percent chance?
I’m not saying that. But -- we’ve all done bad shit. What if -- she’s just fucked up like all of us, trying to do right by her kid?

What’s insane is our solution to every problem is murder. I used to freak out at the sight of blood. Now I barely blink at it. It shouldn’t be like that, this isn’t some fucking Vought movie. Violence isn’t brave, vengeance isn’t brave. But forgiveness, letting go, a little fucking mercy? That’s brave. Crazy but brave. It’s about the last thing my Dad ever taught me, and I just think -- if we’re ever gonna win against monsters, I think we gotta start acting human. MOTHER’S MILK Fuck it.
Fair. Got it. Thanks.
Annie --

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: So, uh... hi everybody.

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Great. So then -- you’re gonna help us take down Vought. And Homelander.

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Butcher...?

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Just hold on. It’s all good.

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: I know how this looks. But everything we’ve been through together, I’ve never once asked you to trust me, but I’m asking now. Like you used to trust your brother. Please, Butcher.

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Stop!

lines.scene: INT. VOUGHT FRESH FARMS FACILITY - DAY
lines.dialogue: No, it’s suicide.
